* No one, whether Jew or Gentile, is without this law that is in men by nature. God gave man all the feelings and senses by which he can struggle to remain in virtue and grow in it. Besides this, God implanted in him the power of reason, by which he perceives what he ought to do and what he ought to avoid. God gave this to all alike.

entries.section: 2. The wicked do not necessarily perish in the world

paragraphs.text: Origen "Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat?" [11]

It is fitting for the ear not to believe everything it hears, but to distinguish between truth and falsehood, as the mouth distinguishes between sweet and bitter. And if the ear, like the mouth, needs to discern what is set before it, whether in hearing or in food, is it not fitting for man to bear a spirit of discernment, to know sound teachings from unsound (1 Cor 10:15; 11:13)?

* He is not speaking of the ear of the body, but the ear of the spirit. With bodily ears we hear the sounds of words, but with the inward ears we distinguish thought and words. Likewise [the palate (especially taste) tasteth his meat], that is, it appreciates it with regard to its pleasantness. So the palate of the spirit discerns its benefit.

Father Hesychius of Jerusalem * [For the mind νοῦς (nous) discerns words]... If God gives us the palate to discern the taste of food, He also gives us the mind to make our decisions, and time allows us to seek understanding.

St. John Chrysostom * There is one judge who oversees the inner, that is, the power of discernment of the mind, but through fitting ways that keep the five senses distinct. God works wonders, so the eye cannot hear, nor the ear see, nor the mouth smell, nor the nose taste, nor the hands smell. While all these work through the powers of the one mind, yet no sense can practice other than what the Creator has assigned to it. And so through these outward bodily arrangements, it is left to us to gather them inwardly in a spiritual way...

While there is one wisdom dwelling in one man less than in another... yet in itself it carries no differences among them, but by it we practice various and different operations, so one receives the gift of wisdom, another the gift of knowledge, another tongues, another the gift of healing...

The blessed Job condemns the inexperience of his friends, and the insolence of everyone who swells up claiming to have been taught in wisdom. For to know something about God is one thing, and to taste what you know with understanding is another.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* There is not one virtue that we can obtain by our human effort unless divine grace helps us. And we see in the Holy Bible that discernment is counted among the gifts of the Spirit, for the Apostle says: "For to one is given by the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit; to another faith by the same Spirit; to another the gifts of healing by the same Spirit... to another discerning of spirits"...

You have seen then how the gift of discernment is not an earthly gift, nor is it a trifling matter, but it is a great gift bestowed by divine grace. If a man does not strive with all zeal after discernment... he will surely err and become like one in the darkness of night and the gloom of obscurity, and he falls not only into snares and passions but errs even in easy matters...

Discernment teaches a man to walk in the royal way, not allowing him extremism on the right in virtue, that is, exaggeration and exceeding the bounds of moderation in boldness and insolence, nor allowing him laziness...

This is the discernment which the Holy Bible expresses by "the eye" or "the light of the body," as the Savior says: "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness.." (Mt 22:6, 23). For it is that which discerns all thoughts and deeds, and sees everything and watches what will happen.

So if a man's eye is "evil," that is, not fortified by the voice of wisdom and knowledge, deceived by some errors and arrogance (in worship), it makes our body "full of darkness." Our minds are darkened and our deeds are in the darkness of vice and the gloom of disturbances, and as He says: "If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!" (Mt 23:6).

No one can doubt that when "the judgment in matters" in the heart is mistaken, that is, when the heart is full of ignorance, our thoughts and deeds, which are the fruit of discernment and contemplation, are in the darkness of the greatest sin.
Abba Moses

12 "With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding. 13 With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding. 14 Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening. 15 Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth. 16 With him is strength and understanding: the deceived and the deceiver are his. 17 He leadeth counsellors away captive, and maketh the judges fools. 18 He looseth the girdles of kings, and bindeth their loins with a cord. 19 He leadeth priests away captive, and overthroweth the mighty. 20 He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the taste of the aged. 21 He poureth contempt upon the nobles, and looseneth the girdle of the strong. 22 He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death. 23 He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and driveth them out. 24 He taketh away the minds of the chiefs of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way. 25 They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man.
"With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding" [12].

No one can deny that some enjoy wisdom, which they receive with the experience of the years and length of days. "How beautiful is wisdom in the aged, and understanding and counsel to men of honour" (Sir 25:7).
They may have wisdom, perception and understanding of matters, yet they are unable to carry out their wisdom, whereas God is all-wise and all-powerful.

Perhaps Job wanted to declare to them that they had been hasty in judging him because they saw him falling into many trials. It would have been fitting for them to wait for a period of time so that, with true wisdom, they might see what lies behind the trials.

St. John Chrysostom says in the person of Job: [Do we, because we know this much, think that we know everything? I know that the wicked are punished, but you see that, in spite of my righteousness, I too am punished. Besides this, does the matter require time for you to understand something that has so many similar examples? Do you not see how the Holy Bible presents depth of experience? What the ancients acquired by experience of events in detail, you who are younger than they offer many thanks to the one who recounts the events. Many sorrows came upon them, and from many sides; and you also, if you search the Holy Scriptures with great care, will see many of them (who entered into afflictions). This is the reason for the saying of one: "Be willing to listen to a good discourse," and in another place he says: [Despise not the discourse of the ancients... for of them thou shalt learn understanding] (Sir 6:35; 8:8-9). You do not need time; for if God Himself wishes to give it to you, you are in no need of time.]

* [With the ancient is wisdom; and in length of days understanding] [12]. This is because we acquire wisdom by study, and learning is planted in the mind by the lessons of men. With God it is otherwise, for He Himself is Wisdom in His person, and He is the One who teaches the lessons of wisdom.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * These sayings establish the roots of wisdom, for as life continues wisdom is strengthened, through the practice of works. But since there are many to whom length of life has been given, and wisdom has not been given, it appears fitting that He who has the decision to give these gifts says: [With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding].
Pope Gregory (the Great)
With him is wisdom and strength,
he hath counsel and understanding [13].
God, who alone is all-wise, perceives all things and is able to accomplish His will, for He is also all-powerful. There is no comparison between the wisdom of the aged and the wisdom of God.
"Give me wisdom, that sitteth by thy throne; and reject me not from among thy children" (Wis 9:4).
"For though a man be never so perfect among the children of men, yet if thy wisdom be not with him, he shall be nothing regarded" (Wis 9:6).
"Thy wisdom was with thee, which knoweth thy works, and was present when thou madest the world, and knew what was acceptable in thy sight, and right in thy commandments" (Wis 9:9).
"The word of God most high is the fountain of wisdom; and her ways are everlasting commandments" (Sir 1:5).

* [With him is wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding] [13]. Job did not speak entirely without offering testimony, nor without a defense (of his opinion); rather, he supports his words with the testimony of the creatures, for the beauty of the visible elements proclaims the wisdom of God and His great power.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * The work of the Father, which pervades all existence, is glorified and greatly magnified when every man advances and reaches the highest stature of growth through fellowship with Christ, "Wisdom," "Knowledge" and "Holiness."

The same thing is fulfilled when a man is sanctified and purified and reaches the highest degrees of perfection through fellowship with the Holy Spirit, and so becomes more worthy to receive the grace of wisdom and knowledge, until every stain of defilement and ignorance is removed from him, and he reaches this progress in perfection and purity. In this way the life he has received from God is worthy of God, who intends it to be pure and perfect. Then the creature becomes worthy of this (holy) life (and is made in the likeness of the Creator); for in this way, which the Creator wills for him, man receives from Him the power to exist eternally...

* God cares for the soul [that is, the seat of the faculties, feelings and sensations] in every man, that he may be rational and receive knowledge, and that his intelligence may work in a fitting manner in the midst of the life of the body, so that his feelings and perceptions (Heb 5:14) become sound.
Origen Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again;
he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening [14].

He who possesses God enjoys His wisdom and power working in him; but he who resists the wisdom of God with his human wisdom will meet with nothing but folly. His life is broken down by divine permission, and there is no one who can build it up. Job takes us back to the age of the building of the tower of Babel, where man relied on his own wisdom and power and thought that he was able to resist God. They thought they could build a tower in heaven, but they failed and their energy was scattered. And behold the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah bears witness to the failure of resisting God.

God shuts up by permitting sickness or calamity, or He allows a man to die, so that he enters the grave and does not come out of it. When He shuts up the wicked in hell, who can bring them up from there?

When a man insists on shutting up his heart upon the practice of a sin and does not open it to receive God's grace and support, the sin remains a prisoner in his heart; it reigns over him and leads him while it is in the prison of the closed heart. So it happened with Pharaoh, who refused in his heart to listen to the voice of God through the plagues, and while he made promises with his deceitful mouth, he harbored in his heart violence and resistance to the work of God. Therefore it was said: "But I will harden Pharaoh's heart" (Ex 7:3), by leaving him a prisoner of his evil and violence.

Pope Gregory (the Great) gives us another example of one whose heart became closed, namely Esau. He closed his heart by his own will, through his evil and carelessness, until he sold his birthright for a meal of lentils, saying: [Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?] (Gen 25:32). Esau despised the birthright, and did not repent of this or of his evils, so his heart was shut up in its evil. His father wanted to open this door to give him the blessing before he died (Gen 27:4), but the Lord rejected this son because he did not repent, and the father gave the blessing to the younger son against his will. Esau cried out with a great cry that did not come from a humble, contrite soul, so his repentance became as nothing, unable to draw God's grace to open his heart.

* Almighty God breaks down the heart of man when He abandons it, and builds it up when He fills it; for He does not break down the soul of man by entering into war, but by withdrawing from it. When the heart is left to itself, it goes to nothing, indeed to its own destruction. Therefore, when it happens that the heart of the hearer is not filled with the grace of Almighty God, because of his sins, the preacher offers his counsels to him from outside in vain. Every mouth that speaks then is as if it were mute, unless God utters a voice in the heart from within, He who inspires the words that are presented to the ear. So the prophet says: "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it" (Ps 127:1). Solomon says: [Consider the work of God: for who can make that straight, which he hath made crooked?] (Eccl 7:13)...

Cain was able to enjoy counsels issuing from the voice of God, and yet he could not change. Because of the sin of his evil heart within, God left him, although He addressed words to him from outside to bear witness against him.

Well did he add: "He shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening" [14]. For every man who practices wrong in all his ways, what does he do but make of himself a prison for his conscience? The sense of guilt in the soul may press upon him even if no one accuses him from outside. And if he is left in the blindness of his evil heart by God's judgment, he is like one who has shut himself in, so that he finds no place to flee, and does not deserve to find such a place. For it often happens that persons long to leave their evil habits, but because they are weighed down to the earth by their burden, they shut up the evil habit in the prison and cannot themselves come out of themselves.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* We learn from this (Ps 127:1) that it is not because God is the One who builds that a man sits idle, as though God would build the house for him. Rather, he works and takes care as far as his human abilities allow, but God removes all obstacles and completes the work. Thus man is called to work as much as he can, in earnestness, but it is God who crowns the work with success. Therefore it is fitting for man, rightly and in godliness, to leave the completion of his work to God, and not to another human being. On this basis Paul planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase, for neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth, but God that giveth the increase (1 Cor 3:6-7). In the same way we can say that this depends not on the will of man or his striving, but on the mercies of God.
Origen * We cannot run in the way of God unless we are carried on the wings of the Spirit.
* It is with God's help that we do the good that we practice.
* No one is stronger than he who enjoys heavenly help, just as no one is weaker than he who is deprived of it.
* Let us be stronger than all, imitating Paul, Peter, James and John; for if God's help is absent from us, we cannot resist the most trifling temptation.
* We fear nothing, for in order to defeat Satan we must know that our skill will profit nothing, and that everything is from the grace of God.

* Those who are punished, it is on account of justice; but those who are crowned, it is on account of grace. Even if they had practiced a thousand good works, they enjoy heaven and the Kingdom in return for these small works only by the freedom of grace, and so they are lifted up to what cannot be measured.
St. John Chrysostom Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up:
also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth [15].

The rains are in the hand of God; if He withholds them, the earth dries up and its fruits perish (Job 4:7). And if He allows them in abundance, the flood of sweeping rain destroys the crops of the earth and buildings collapse. Perhaps he refers here to the flood of Noah, when the earth was drowned.

* If He shuts heaven, who can open it? And if He opens the windows of the flood, who can shut them? Who can increase the rain or hold it back from falling in sufficient measure, except the One who governs the universe by His measure and His balances?

St. Gregory of Nazianzus * If you understand "the waters" as the knowledge of preaching, as it is written: "The words of a man's mouth are as deep waters, and the wellspring of wisdom as a flowing brook" (Prov 18:4), then when the waters are withheld everything becomes dry. This means that when the knowledge of the preacher is withheld, the hearts of those who ought to have been refreshed with the hope of eternity dry up. They may remain in the barrenness of hopelessness, through their love of temporal things...

And if the expression "the waters" refers to the gift of the Holy Spirit, as the voice of Truth said in the Gospel: "He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water," adding: "This spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive" (Jn 7:38-39)... then when the Holy Spirit is withheld from the mind of the hearer, the sense at once becomes dry, which through hope seemed green in the hearer.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

Pope Gregory (the Great) says: [When Paul was on his way to Damascus, armed with letters against Christ, he was watered on his journey by the grace of the Holy Spirit, and was immediately changed from his intention to shed blood; and afterward he received for Christ's sake the blows that on his journey he had wished to pour out upon the Christians. He who before, walking according to the flesh, strove to deliver the saints of the Lord to death, came to rejoice to offer the sacrifice of his body for the life of the saints. He who was cold, aiming at cruelty, was turned into the warmth of tenderness; and he who was formerly a blasphemer and persecutor became a humble preacher full of tenderness. He who counted the slaughter of Christ in His disciples a great gain, [now holds fast to Christ to be his life, counting death gain] (Phil 1:21). So [he sendeth out the waters, and they overturn the earth] [15], in the mind of Paul, at the moment in which he received the grace of the Holy Spirit, which changed the steadfastness of his obstinacy and cruelty.]
* The first waters brought forth life; let no one marvel if the waters in Baptism can also give life.

* The Spirit of God was borne upon the waters, He who renews the creation of the one who is baptized. The Holy One was borne upon the holy waters, or rather upon the waters that receive holiness from Him. Thus the waters were sanctified by the Spirit and received the possibility of sanctifying. This is the reason why, since the waters were the primary element (of creation), they obtained the mystery of sanctification through the invocation of God.
Tertullian * The new creation is accomplished by water and the Spirit, as in the creation of the world, when the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
St. Clement of Alexandria With him is strength and wisdom:
the deceived and the deceiver are his [16].

He is the One who has power and strength, and He is the source of wisdom and understanding. He cares for all men, even the simple whom others lead astray, and the crafty who lead their brothers astray. He uses all things to accomplish His divine plan, for both the deceiver and the deceived are under His hands. He is glorified in all, although He does not accept error, craftiness and cunning. In the end the believers sing: "Alleluia: for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth" (Rev 19:6).

* If anyone has power and authority, or has acquired understanding and prudence, this is from God; he receives them from Him, who gives generously to those who wish to receive. And it is clear that He takes them back from whom He wishes. Among many, there is an example that teaches you this, namely Nebuchadnezzar, whose power was great, of whom Daniel said: "It is thou, O king, that art grown and become strong: for thy greatness is grown, and reacheth unto heaven, and thy dominion to the end of the earth" (Dan 4:22). Nevertheless, since he exalted himself in pride on every occasion, he lost not only his authority and kingdom, but also knowledge and understanding, [and was driven from men, and did eat grass as oxen] (Dan 4:33). He came to think like a beast, and not as men think. Why did this happen to him? Daniel explained this very clearly: "Seven times shall pass over thee, till thou know that the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will" (Dan 4:25). And when (Nebuchadnezzar) knew this, he recovered his spirit, and at the same time his kingship, when he offered praise and glory to God (Dan 4:34-37).
Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools [17].
Not only individuals are under His authority, but even the movements of nations and peoples do not escape the hands of the Ruler of all.

He often allows fools who think themselves wise counsellors to fall into captivity like spoils of war, robbed of their dignity, wealth and freedom; they are robbed not only of their wisdom but sometimes, as it were, of their humanity.

Even judges who are known for their counsel and the loftiness of their thoughts sometimes become fools, just as God made foolish the counsel of Ahithophel, who became true to his name, for it means "brother of folly or stupidity." As it was said by Isaiah: "The princes of Zoan are become fools; the princes of Noph are deceived; and they that are the chiefs of her tribes have led Egypt astray" (Isa 19:13).

Often the aged, who have long experience and wisdom, lose their ability to understand; the very factor of time that led them to wisdom is the one that causes the weakness of old age, and returns them to a state resembling childhood, like one who has neither experience nor understanding.

* [He leadeth counsellors away to a foolish end] [17], that is, when they do good without a good purpose, but seek temporal reward. For if the only Son of God the Father, the Most High, became man to preach eternal truths, and for this reason was called [the Angel of Great Counsel] (Isa 9:6), then we rightly interpret "the counsellors" as the preachers who supply their hearers with the counsel of life. But when any preacher proclaims eternal truths in order to gain temporal profits, he surely [goes to a foolish end], since he aims to attain that by his wearisome labors, from which an upright mind ought to flee.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
* The thought of "vainglory" is the most wicked of all kinds of thoughts.

This thought comes to those who walk in the life of righteousness, and the man begins to glorify his own striving and to gather for himself the praise of others. He imagines the demons' terror of him, his healing of women, the crowds thronging around him touching the hem of his garment, and finally he foresees his own consecration to the priesthood, and that people will come to him to make him a priest, and when he refuses the priesthood they bind him and lead him against his will.

After Satan has kindled in him these false hopes, he withdraws, leaving the field to other battles brought by the demon of pride or the demon of murmuring, who comes at once and presents him with thoughts contrary to these hopes, so that at times he surrenders to the thoughts of the demon of fornication, he who a few moments before saw himself as a saint and a venerable priest!

As for the "demon of pride," he is the cause of the soul's most grievous fall. He advises the soul not to look to God as its helper, but to attribute to itself everything that is good. Then it begins to swell up before the brethren and reckons them ignorant, because they do not know its lofty rank.
Pride is followed by anger and murmuring. And the last evil is followed by the man's losing his senses, by fury, and by seeing many demons in the air.

*It is hard for you to escape the thought of vainglory, because everything you do to drive it away can become a helping factor in creating a new motive toward vainglory. Moreover, the demons do not always resist every sound thought, but sometimes they encourage in us some sound thoughts in the hope that afterward they can deceive us.
St. Evagrius He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle [18].

God sometimes permits those in authority, such as kings, to be brought down from their positions and stripped of all honor. He looses their belts, so the sword falls from their side and the crowns from their heads. Perhaps he refers here to their descent to become slaves, since slaves did not gird their loins.
He leadeth priests away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty [19].

Having spoken of the classes of the wise, such as counsellors and judges, of the classes of those with experience, such as the aged, and of the classes of those with authority, such as kings, he now speaks of those who think themselves righteous, namely the class of priests. These, in their hypocrisy, sometimes think that they cannot be touched because they are servants of God and work on behalf of His people. But God has no partiality; even His priests He allows to be taken captive, and they lose their dignity, their authority and the wealth in which they took pride.

Finally he refers to the class of the mighty: the strong man quickly becomes weak. How many men of mighty strength have fallen into the trap of weak men, and how many strong armies have been defeated before armies weaker than they. So it is not fitting for anyone to rely on his temporal strength, nor on his own wisdom and mere human understanding, nor his authority, nor his social or religious position.

* [He leadeth priests away to shame, and overthroweth the mighty] [19]. The great glory of the priest is the righteousness of those subject to him. The excellent preacher rightly says to his disciples: "For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of rejoicing? Are not even ye in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?" (1 Thess 2:19). But priests neglect the lives of those entrusted to them, and do not bear fruit as they advance before the Lord. Thus they come into shame, finding no glory before the strict Judge, those who do not seek Him in the lives of those they serve through their urgency in preaching.

Well did he say: "and overthroweth the mighty." By a just judgment He leaves the hearts of those who rule, if they do not look to the inward reward, and they are cast out, where they deceive themselves by rejoicing in temporal glory instead of eternal.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

*The fault is not in authority in itself, but in vain covetousness. Accordingly, the establishment of authority comes from God, and whoever exercises it is an ambassador of God, being God's minister for good (Rom 13:3-4). The act in itself is not sin, but the fault lies in the one who carries it out... We must distinguish between the good use of authority and the bad use.
St. Ambrose He removeth away the speech of the trusted, and taketh away the understanding of the aged [20].

When those who excel in eloquence, oratory and philosophies take pride in their linguistic creativity or the attractiveness of their personalities, they sometimes stand as mutes, with not a word in their mouth, because they insulted Him who gave them the mind and granted them the gift of speech and created their mouths.

* [He changeth the lips of the trusted, and taketh away the teachings of the aged] [20]. When the priest does not practice the good that he proclaims, the very work of his lips is taken from him, so that he does not dare to utter what he does not practice. It was said by the prophet: "But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?" (Ps 50:16). Likewise he asks Him: "And take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth" (Ps 119:43). For it appears that Almighty God gives the word of truth to those who practice it, and takes it away from those who do not practice it...

The Truth says in the Gospel: "For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things" (Mt 12:34-35)... Likewise John says: "They are of the world: therefore speak they of the world" (1 Jn 4:5). Well was it said: [He who changeth the lips of the trusted, and taketh away the teachings of the aged].
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* "A bishop then must be blameless" (d)... All the virtues are contained in this phrase, and so it seems as if the Apostle demands an impossible perfection. For if any sin or any idle word deserves blame, who in this world is without sin and without blame? And yet he who is chosen as shepherd of the Church must be distinguished from the others, who in truth are a flock of (rational) sheep.

If the eloquent define the orator as [a good man skilled in speaking], since he must be without fault in his conduct as in his lips (his oratory) in order to be worthy of praise, because the teacher whose words are not supported by his deeds loses all influence over his hearers.

St. Jerome * "Blameless"... This phrase contains all the virtues, so that if a man knows of some sin in himself, it is not good for him to covet an office for which he is not qualified; rather he needs a guide, and not to act as a guide. For he who plays a leading role must be more radiant than any shining star. His life must be without fault, and all look to him and imitate his conduct.

St. John Chrysostom Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that this phrase applies to the Jews, whose lips uttered the truth before the Incarnation of the Word; they believed that He was coming, and proclaimed His coming, but their lips changed after His coming, and they denied Him. He became present in their midst, He whose coming they had proclaimed beforehand. But they took away the teachings of their fathers, since they did not walk according to what their fathers prophesied to them about Him.
He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty [21].
When the honorable insult their Creator, they reap contempt for themselves. "He poureth contempt upon princes, and causeth them to wander in the wilderness, where there is no way" (Ps 107:40).

* [He poureth contempt upon princes, and raiseth up the persecuted] [21]. The Jewish people continued in the commandment of the Law, while the whole Gentile world knew nothing of the commandment of God; the former were called honorable through faith, while the others fell into the passion of unbelief. But when Judaism denied the mystery of the Incarnation of our Lord, and the Gentile world believed in Him, the honorable fell into contempt, and those who had descended into the sin of unbelief were raised up and received the freedom of the true faith. Jeremiah, seeing this long before it happened, said: "The Lord was as an enemy: he hath swallowed up Israel, he hath swallowed up all his palaces: he hath destroyed his strong holds" (Lam 2:5).
Pope Gregory (the Great)
* When God rejected Israel, grace flowed to the Gentiles; the calling of the Gentiles began with the fall of Israel, and they receive by the grace of God Jesus Christ, whom the prophets had foretold.

* We Christians say that the Jews, though they previously enjoyed God's favor, being loved by Him more than others, yet this divine dispensation and grace have been transferred to us, when Jesus transferred the authority that worked among the Jews to the believers from the Gentiles.
Origen He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death [22].

When the first man fell into disobedience, death came to accompany his mind like a shadow, indeed more closely attached than a shadow. Nothing terrifies him like death, so that the Apostle Paul called it "the last enemy," or the most violent enemy that confronts man. But the death of the Lord Christ on the Cross destroyed the power of death in its own lair. By death He trampled death, and granted us the power of eternal life and resurrection.

The Lord Christ removed the expression "death" from the dictionary of our thought, and in its place came the expression "the shadow of death," or "sleep," or "departure." We sing, saying: "There is no death for Your servants, but a departure." And we chant with the Apostle Paul, saying: "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?" (1 Cor 15:55).

The Lord exposed death, so that it became a shadow without substance in the lives of those who believe in Him. He shone with His light upon the tombs, and the weakness of the shadow of death was exposed.
The Lord lifted the covering from the darkness, and we realized that we have no place in the kingdom of darkness, since the Sun of Righteousness has shone upon us.

God exposes the plots that are devised in darkness, and the evil that is committed in secret. When the king of Aram thought that there was a traitor among his men, one of his servants said to him: "Elisha, the prophet that is in Israel, telleth the king of Israel the words that thou speakest in thy bedchamber" (2 Kgs 6:12).

* [He discovereth deep things out of darkness] [22]. What are the deep things? The hidden matters, the thoughts that do not appear in the brightness of the day. This is the reason that Job speaks of darkness. For Christ Himself uses the same words to affirm and confirm the words of Job when He says to the Apostles: "For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known" (Mt 10:26). Remember the words He added: "What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops" (Mt 10:27).

"And bringeth out to light the shadow of death" [22]. The shadow of death is sin, in the same way that the shadow reveals the body that casts the shadow; so sin means [The sting of death is sin] (1 Cor 15:56), and it is its distinguishing characteristic.

In any case, this shadow of death makes known its mystery (Rom 16:25; Col 1:26) to mankind, and makes known its righteousness (Ps 98:2; Rom 1:17); in the same manner it uncovers sin (Eph 4:22) and does not allow it to be hidden. And since we know its ugliness and that it corrupts the soul, let us all flee from it! This is the reason that Christ said of the Jewish people: "If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin" (Jn 15:22), in other words, they would not have known the power of sin. But He adds: "but now they have no cloke for their sin," because they knew its defilement, its evil smell and its wickedness when compared with the righteousness and beauty that had not been known before.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem Pope Gregory (the Great) sees in the shadow of death a reference to the severity of the Law, which stressed that everyone who sins deserves the death of the body; but when the Savior came He removed the death of the body as a penalty for the one who commits sin, and directed our eyes to the seriousness of the working of sin on our souls.
He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them:
he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them again (scattereth them) [23].

God is the Ruler of all history; He sometimes allows some to grow and have authority to achieve a certain aim for the discipline of His people, as happened with Babylon, which was a small state that soon defeated great Assyria and took its place, and carried Judah into captivity; and when Babylon exalted itself against God, in moments it collapsed and was taken by Persia and Media. She who was the head became the tail, and even vanished.

* [He maketh the nations to wander and destroyeth them; he scattereth them and then bringeth them in] [23]... It is not He who leads the nations away, but He allows them to wander; they go of themselves to destruction through their evils, since they do not wish to return to faith in Him. As for the scattered nations, Job would say to the Lord: "Scatter them," while He wishes to lead those who desire to run toward the light (Isa 60:3) to enjoy the preaching. He will not transgress justice, but acts as is fitting with each one, whether in faith or in unbelief. Therefore, when Simeon took the Lord, the Child, in his arms, he said: "This child is set for the fall and rising again of many" (Lk 2:34).
Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way [24].

Who are the chiefs of the earth who lose their understanding, if not the sons of Abraham according to the flesh, who withdrew from their spiritual sonship to him by denying the Savior of the world, and rejecting Him whose day their father Abraham rejoiced to see, many generations before His coming?
Their denial turned their lives into a barren wilderness, where their hearts are not watered by the waters of the Holy Spirit, who turns the wildernesses into a divine paradise!

* [He changeth the hearts of the chiefs of the people of the earth] [24]. By the words "people of the earth" a man needs to understand the Jewish people, because they clung to earthly things. Paul also spoke of those who [set their minds on earthly things]. Their chiefs are the priests, the scribes and the Pharisees. By the changing of their hearts he means that He turns them.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * For since there remained for them no altar, no temple and no priest, and therefore they had no sacrificial offerings, they felt that their sin remained in them, and that there was no way for them to obtain forgiveness.

Origen * Behold, Samaritans and Galileans have believed in Christ, to the shame and confusion of the Jews; and the Samaritans were found better than the Galileans, because those Samaritans received Him from the word of the woman, while the Galileans received Him because of His miracles. The Evangelist reminds the hearer of the miracle (the turning of water into wine at Cana of Galilee) to raise the praise of the Samaritans, for the men of Cana received Him because of the miracle that was done in Jerusalem, and this was not the case with the Samaritans, who received Him on account of His teaching alone.
St. John Chrysostom They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man [25].

Those who were leaders of great peoples, with their military power and their fearful authority, soon lost everything and came into humiliation and weakness. As the Psalmist says: "The stouthearted are spoiled... none of the men of might have found their hands" (Ps 76:5). They became like those who are lost "in a wilderness where there is no way" [24]. They feel for the way in the darkness and stagger like drunkards, without consciousness, without thought, and without strength.
Thus Job speaks of God, the Ruler of all, in the grasp of whose hand is all history, turning events to the account of His Kingdom. No power can resist Him!

* Why? Because they [loved darkness rather than light] (Jn 3:19), in such a way that the Lord Himself became their accuser. Why did they love darkness rather than light? Because their deeds are evil. For it is inevitable that those who practice evils [stagger like a drunken man]. For like drunkards they are befuddled, unable to distinguish between one thing and another, or between evil and good.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * O company of the Jews, when you come to Jerusalem and find that it has been laid waste and turned to dust and ashes, do not weep like children (1 Cor 4). Do not grieve, but seek for yourselves a city in heaven instead of the one you seek here on earth. Lift up your eyes, and you will find on high the Jerusalem which is free, which is the mother of us all (Gal 4:26).

Do not grieve over the absence of the temple here, nor despair over your lack of a priest. For in heaven you will find an altar and priests of the good things to come, after the order of Melchizedek, in their procession before God (Heb 5:10). For the love and mercy of the Lord willed to remove from you the earthly inheritance, so that you might seek the heavenly.
Origen
You have granted me wisdom to glorify You, not to examine Your works!
* Glory to You, O Giver of mind, thought, heart and all human faculties!
It is not for me to exalt myself over Your creation, my brothers in humanity.
You are wonderful in Your wisdom, distributing all gifts to mankind.
Grant me a holy mind, and a heart that bears You within it.
Sanctify my whole being, sanctify my thought and my heart.
Lift up my thought, O Lord, by Your Spirit, that I may honor every colleague of mine.
Fill my heart, that it may open wide with love for every human being.
* My God, how my soul is embittered by the mockery of my loved ones!
I have become to them a byword and a laughingstock!
But I look to You, and I see You wounded in the house of Your loved ones!
My soul rejoices and glorifies You, for You have allowed me to share in Your sufferings!
I have truly understood that in wisdom You allowed my loved ones to wound me!
I accept these wounds as a crown of glory that I do not deserve.
In the midst of the bitterness of my soul I feel for Your comforting hand.
I understand that every mockery that befalls me is by Your permission.
In Your wondrous love You wanted me to share with You in Your reproaches!
I see that darkness cannot bear the light.
And corruption thinks that it is able to destroy incorruption.
And the fallen devil thinks that he has authority!
Glory to You, who turn my sufferings into a joyful hymn, so that I see the earnest of heaven revealed in my depths.
Let me realize, O Lord, that Your plan for me is surpassing.
Then I will rejoice in my brothers' mockery of me.
While they mock me, the heavenly ones see me in surpassing glory!
Surely these temporary moments will soon pass, and I will pass with You into the bosom of Your Father, and enjoy fellowship in heavenly glory!
The winter with its snow will pass, and the spring of eternity will come with its splendor.
* My God, You have granted mankind wisdom and understanding to glorify You.
Behold, even creation bears witness to Your wisdom, Your love and Your care!
Creation, visible and hidden, glorifies You!
All bear witness to Your incomprehensible wisdom.
* Grant me to worship at Your feet.
With all my heart I praise You for what I know of You, or what I do not yet know.
Truly, I stand perplexed before Your wisdom; I see wicked men and robbers who think themselves kings and gods.
They live a prosperous, successful life, while Your children suffer as if heavenly wrath had come upon them!
Who can comprehend Your wisdom, O Wise and Almighty One?
* Behold, all nature preaches to me:
Submit to your heavenly Father, who loves you and cares for you.
In His hands is all your life; for your sake He brought us into being, and behold, He is preparing a place for you in His divine bosom.
Do not rely on your personal experiences alone; your Creator alone gives you wisdom, and reveals to you the understanding of His mysteries.
Submit, for by your humility you are raised to the heights.
Do not resist and do not contend; does the clay resist its Creator?
Who gave you the mouth to speak, the ear to hear, and the hand to touch?
Who gave you mind, thought, wisdom and understanding?
He loves you; your life and all your gifts are His gifts to you!
* My God, who is there to support me but You?
Kings, emperors and rulers exalted themselves, and were filled with shame!
Strong nations and peoples exalted themselves, and fell before weak nations.
My God, grant me the spirit of discernment, that I may walk as Your son!
Glory to You, who loved me before I came into being.
You shatter my ignorance and folly, and grant me the wisdom that is with You!
You dispel my darkness, and grant me Your surpassing light!
You put my death to death, and grant me Your glorious resurrection!
You expose the devil and his hosts, and cast them under my feet!
You give me Yourself, so that I lack nothing!

1 "Lo, mine eye hath seen all this, mine ear hath heard and understood it. 2 What ye know, the same do I know also: I am not inferior unto you. 3 Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God."
Lo, mine eye hath seen all this,
mine ear hath heard and understood it [1].

* See how, even in his humility, what he proclaimed was symbolic, led by the prophetic Spirit, who reveals to him what is higher. For he says, "Mine eye hath seen all this"; it is clear that he speaks a prophetic vision. "Mine ear hath heard it": the one whom God finds holy He chooses to hear His mysteries.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * "And understood it"... When something is seen or heard about without understanding being granted to the man, it is no longer a prophetic vision. Pharaoh saw in a dream things that were to happen to Egypt, but he could not understand what he saw, and he was not a prophet. King Belshazzar saw the fingers of a hand writing on the wall, yet he was not a prophet, because he did not obtain the understanding of what he saw.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
What ye know, the same do I know also:
I am not inferior unto you [2].
The humble Job was obliged to defend himself and to praise himself, as the Apostle Paul did later, when some groups in Corinth made the accusation that he was not an apostle.
Here Job affirms that he is not inferior to them, and that what they know he knew also; in these circumstances he does not need sermons and discussions, but love, care and prayers to support him.

* May we not be strenuous in debate and slothful in our prayers (for them). Let us pray, dear beloved, let us pray that God may give us grace, even for our enemies, and especially for our brethren and loved ones.
St. Augustine Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God [3].

He turned away from his friends and turned toward God, for he found no rest in speaking with them; therefore he wanted to speak with the Almighty, for to be judged before God is better than to fall into the hand of a man. To enter into dialogue with God is easier than dialogue with friends. As David said to Gad the prophet: "I am in a great strait: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for his mercies are great: and let me not fall into the hand of man" (2 Sam 24:14; 1 Chr 21:13).

* I also know the infinite greatness of God, the unlimited wisdom of the Creator, and His amazing power; but with this knowledge [I desire to speak to the Lord], for I know His righteousness. Since He is righteous, He bears with those who speak with Him without being accused. For if He does not wish this, I will be silent, since I know what I am bound to as one who receives the honor of being His servant. By His command "I speak," and I dare to the point of accusing God.
Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * I will not cease speaking with God, for am I speaking with a man? I speak with God, who knows the secrets of my thoughts.
He says that it is a matter of great value to be judged before God rather than to be judged before them.

St. John Chrysostom * We speak to the Almighty when we ask for His tenderness, and we argue with Him (are judged before God) when we unite with Him in His righteousness and examine our works with careful inquiry. Perhaps by arguing with God he means that whoever obeyed God's commandments here will come with Him as a judge when He judges the people (Mt 19:28)... Therefore the Lord also says through Isaiah: "Relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. Come now, and let us reason together" (Isa 1:17-18).

For it is right that they should plead with God concerning the charges in the judgment, those who at (hearing) the words of God utterly renounce the present world. Thus speaking with Him is fulfilled by prayer, and pleading with Him by judgment.

Therefore the saint speaks here with the Almighty, so that he may afterward plead with Him (at the time of the general judgment), when he comes afterward with God as a judge, he who clings to the Almighty here by prayer.

As for the holy Church, to which we said before that Job bears a likeness that is to come, she not only judges the wicked when the time of the final judgment arrives, but even now does not cease to judge all, whether those who walk in evil or those who think foolishly.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

4 "But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value. 5 O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom. 6 Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips. 7 Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him? 8 Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?"
But ye are forgers of lies,
ye are all physicians of no value [4].

Job complains of his friends, because they judged him and condemned him according to their false notions and their lack of understanding of God's providence and care and His plan for mankind. Therefore they became forgers of lies. They uttered falsehood and fabricated false accusations against him.

They came to him as physicians to attend to his wounds, but in truth they were physicians of no value; they did not know the disease, so the treatment turned out deadly. They changed from wise physicians into charlatan quacks. They claimed science and knowledge, while in complete ignorance of the divine truth, because they had lost love.

Job did not accept his brothers as physicians offering him the cure, looking instead to the coming Messiah, as the heavenly Physician of souls and bodies, who heals the eyes of our souls so that they enjoy the vision of divine things.

Wonderful is our heavenly Physician, for when He declared Himself a physician He was eating in the house of a tax collector, with many tax collectors and sinners gathered around Him. He did not preach to them nor rebuke them for their sins, but He ate with them (Lk 5:27-32). I do not think I would find a doctor who enters a hospital and invites all the patients to eat with him, then leaves them and goes out of the hospital without giving them medicines specific to their diseases to heal them.

The Lord gave the medicine when He ate with them, for He gave them practical love; He ate with those whom society loathed and did not even want to deal with, lest it be defiled. The Holy One stretches out His hand and eats with them, so that they may realize that their Savior is not far from them, nor aloof from them. This is the heavenly medicine that the heavenly Physician offered. He is a unique Physician and His medicine is unique!

And the wonder is that He declared His person thus as a physician at the very moments when He declared that His disciples are the children of the bridechamber, or friends of the Bridegroom. As though those who work with Him have as their work to receive the mysteries of the Bridegroom, so as to proclaim His person, His characteristics and His abilities to the bride: the humanity that accepts faith in Him. As though those who work with the Physician have no work except preparing for the joyful heavenly wedding.

The work of the servant of the Lord Christ, and of all leaders, indeed of every Christian, is to contribute to the preparation for this wedding, not by rebuke, reproof and condemnation, but by revealing the love of the Bridegroom and His coming down to His bride, and opening the doors of heaven, her bridal chamber, to her. For the bride is prepared for her Bridegroom by discovering her Bridegroom's love for her and His longing for her.

* You are harmful physicians who renew the diseases, [you renew evil], you who do not bring healing from the wounds by using very fitting remedies. So you think that you are defending God, and that your mouth utters pleasing words; yet you see evils in the one placed on trial, and you come to help the enemy by stirring up feelings of pain in the wounded.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * The heavenly Guide, the Logos, is called the Leader when He calls mankind to salvation... But when He works as a physician or trainer, His name becomes "the Instructor"... For the sick soul needs an instructor who heals its passions. Then it needs the Teacher who gives it understanding... "the revelation of the Logos." Thus, since the Logos wishes our salvation step by step, He uses an excellent method: at first He leads, then He corrects, and finally He teaches.

* Who is He? Learn briefly that He is the Word of truth, the Word of incorruption, who renews man by restoring him to the truth. He is the goad that urges to salvation. He is the destroyer of perdition and the driver away of death. He builds the temple of God in men, taking them for God as a dwelling.

The sick need a savior, the lost need a guide, the blind need one who leads them to the light, the thirsty need the living fountain from which whoever drinks will never thirst, the dead need life, the sheep need a shepherd, and children need a teacher; all mankind needs Jesus!

St. Clement of Alexandria * Blessed indeed are those who in their need of the Son of God have gone beyond the need of Him as a physician to heal their diseases, or as a shepherd, or as a redeemer, and whose need of Him has become need of Him as Wisdom and as Logos, or as one of the other titles He offers to those who have the spiritual Pascha that prepares them for the highest graces.
* Within the divinity of the Word there is power, not only to help and heal those who are sick..., but to reveal mysteries to those who are pure in body and mind.
The Word was sent as a physician to sinners, and also as a teacher to those who are already pure and without sin.

* By the light of the Word the darkness of heretical teachings is dispelled. For the Word opens the eyes of our souls, so that we can distinguish between light and darkness, and in every case choose to remain in the light.
* He who seeks healing has no course but to follow Jesus.
* Come now to Jesus, the heavenly Physician.
Enter this clinic, which is His Church.

Look. There lie great numbers of the weak. You find a woman seeking cleansing (Mk 5:25; Lev 12). You also find a leper isolated "without the camp" because of the defilement of his leprosy (Mk 1:40; Lev 13:46).
They seek healing from the Physician, asking how they may become healthy and how they may be cleansed.
Jesus the Physician is Himself the Word of God. He prepares medicines for His patients, not from preparations of herbs, but from the holy things of words.

If someone looks at those medicines of words scattered without order in the folds of the books, and does not know the power of the individual words, he may perhaps turn from them as cheap things lacking eloquence. But he who knows that the medicine of souls is in Christ will certainly understand from these books that are read in the Church how every person must gather useful herbs from the fields and mountains, I mean the power of the words, so that he who is troubled in soul may obtain healing, not by the power of the outer branches (of medicinal plants) and the surface bark, so much as by the effectiveness of the inner sap.

* There are also many other things hidden from us, known only to Him who is the Physician of our souls. For as regards our bodily health, we find it sometimes necessary to take disagreeable and bitter medicines as a cure for diseases we have brought upon ourselves through food and drink. So it happens if the nature of the disease requires harsh treatment with the surgeon's knife in a painful operation. Yes, and if the disease happens to extend beyond the effect of these remedies, recourse is had in the end to where the disease must be cauterized with fire. How can we realize that God, our Physician, desires to wash away the diseases of our souls that many sins and crimes have brought upon us, and uses a corrective treatment of similar kinds that may extend to the point of imposing the punishment of fire on those who have lost the health of their souls.
Origen * First, that you may realize God's condescension. Condescend and be humble for your own sakes, looking to God who condescended in humility also for your sake and not for His own...
Confess your weakness; and lie before the Physician in patience.
When you realize His condescension you are lifted up with Him, not by His raising Himself as the Word, but rather by being understood by you more and more...
He does not increase, but you are the ones who advance, so that He is as one who has risen with you...

Look at the tree: it first sends its roots down so that it may grow upward. It fixes its lower root in the earth so that its top may extend to heaven. Does it make any effort to grow except through humility? Then "that Christ may dwell in your hearts by faith; that ye, being rooted and grounded in love... might be filled with all the fulness of God" (Eph 3:17-19).

St. Augustine * We see that the Holy Scripture does not present the Lord to us under one name, nor only under the names assigned to His divinity or indicating His greatness; sometimes it uses the distinctions of nature (His hypostatic properties), and knows to say: [the name which is above every name] (Phil 2:9), the name of the Son, and the true Son, and the only-begotten God the Son, and the power of God and His wisdom and His Word. And sometimes, considering the multitude of ways by which grace comes to us, which in His goodness He grants to those who seek it according to His wisdom of many aspects, Scripture calls Him by many other titles. It calls Him at one time the Shepherd, at another the King, then the Physician, the Bridegroom, the Way, the Door, the Fountain, the Bread, the Axe and the Rock. These names do not indicate the nature, as I said, but the multiplicity of the activity that He exerts, out of mercy to each one of His creatures, and in answer to the need of everyone who asks Him.

St. Basil the Great * There is one Physician, who is at the same time flesh and spirit (man and God), begotten γεννητός: gennetos, and unbegotten, God become man. True life in death (in a mortal body), He was mortal (in the flesh) and is now immortal (by His resurrection), of Mary and of God, He is Jesus Christ our Lord.

St. Ignatius Theophorus * Let us then worship Him as God, believing in His becoming man, for what profit is there in saying of Him that He is a man and not God, or what salvation is there for us if we refuse to confess His humanity along with His divinity? Let us confess His presence, for He is King and Physician. For Jesus the King, having become a Physician, girded Himself with the linen of our humanity, and healed what was sick. The perfect Teacher of babes became a babe among them (Rom 2:20), that He might give wisdom to the foolish. The Bread of heaven came down to earth to feed the hungry!

* "Jesus" means "Savior," but in Greek it means "the Healer," for He is the Physician of souls and bodies, the Healer of spirits; He opened the eyes of the man born blind, and led minds to the light. He heals the visibly lame, and leads sinners in the way of repentance. He says to the paralytic: "Sin no more," and also: "Take up thy bed, and walk," because the body was paralyzed because of the sin of the soul. He served the soul first so that He might extend healing to the body.
Therefore if any of you is suffering in soul because of his sins, you will find Him a physician for you. And if any of you is of little faith, let him say to Him: "Help thou mine unbelief" (Mk 9:24).
And if any of you is afflicted with bodily pains, let him not be unbelieving, but draw near, for Jesus heals such diseases, and let him know that Jesus is the Christ.

St. Cyril of Jerusalem * By the Physician's many medicines He grants healing... He binds up the wounds with firm commandments, and sends forth warmth when He forgives sins. He pricks the heart as wine does, when He announces His judgment. And he set him on his own beast (Lk 10:34); consider how He lifts you up (in Himself), since He bore our sins and suffered for us (Isa 53:4). The Shepherd also carried the lost sheep on His shoulders (Lk 15:5).
St. Ambrose O that ye would altogether hold your peace!
and it should be your wisdom [5].

They came to offer wise counsels, yet it appeared that they themselves rather needed someone to guide them and bring them into wisdom. The wisdom they lacked was that they should altogether hold their peace; their silence is more beneficial than vain, wounding speech. As the wise man says: "Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding" (Prov 17:28).

* [It would have been better, for God's sake, for you to keep silence, and it would be your wisdom] [5]... The wise man is not only one who speaks well, offering useful counsels and declaring what is beneficial and dignified for all, but also one who bridles himself (Jas 3:2)... He observes what David sang in the Psalms: [Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips. Incline not my heart to any evil thing, to practise wicked works with men that work iniquity] (Ps 141:3-4).

Let us withdraw completely from them, even if they sometimes think they are defending God, not with the intention of glorifying God, but to slander the one who dedicates himself to righteousness and to betray the soldier of goodness... For a man needs to flee from deceivers and their friendship, and turn his face away from their flattery. But men of goodness accept the rebuke that comes from them, and remember with dignity their malicious talk against them, for all things turn to their good and work for good (Rom 8:28), and soon they receive the praise of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit...
Job spoke, after losing all his wealth, as though he were in abundance.

Fr. Hesychius of Jerusalem * As in a house, when the door is shut, it is not known which members are hidden in it, so in general, if the fool keeps his peace (his silence), he hides whether he is wise or foolish. So it is when no work comes into the light, the mind speaks even if the man is silent. Therefore the saint, seeing his companions appear as what they are not, commands them to keep their peace (their silence), so that they may not be exposed for what they are. Thus it was said of Solomon: "Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise" (Prov 17:28).
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* [Set a guard, O Lord, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips] (Ps 141:3). He did not say "a fortified barrier," but [a fortified door]. A door is opened as well as shut. If this is a door, let it open and shut. It opens for the confession of sin, and shuts for the forgiveness of sin. For it is a door for protection, not for destruction.
St. Augustine Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips [6].

He calls them to listen to him instead of vain talk. Although they did not interrupt him, they paid no attention to his words, nor did they give heed to the cries of his bitter soul. They thought they had defended God and spoken the truth, but without practical love they do not know God, nor do they perceive the truth.

* [Hear now my rebukes, and give ear to the judgment of my lips] [6]. Well does he begin first by offering rebuke and afterward "judgment." For unless the fool's pride is quenched, he cannot at all understand the judgment of the righteous.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him? [7]

Job mocks them because they thought that God needed them to defend Him and to reveal His justice. As though he says to them: Who are you, weak ones without love, that you should defend the divine truth, which is inseparable from love?

Under the pretext of defending divine justice they spoke deceit, and made false accusations against Job, and counted him wicked, and so fell into lying, cruelty, injustice and wronging their brother. And they justify all this by saying that it is "for God." They did not realize that "the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God" (Jas 1:20).

They justified their evil conduct toward Job as being to achieve a lofty aim, namely the defense of God. Does a good end justify an evil means? As though they were saying: "Let us do evil, that good may come" (Rom 3:8). God rebuked those who hate their brethren while they praise God: "Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed" (Isa 66:5).

He who has fellowship with God, the Truth, cannot practice deceit and lying, unless a man has turned aside from God, who cannot endure deceit. The Psalmist often puts deceit on the same level as the shedding of blood, because its aim is the destruction of the souls of others and their possessions or honor; and the deceiver destroys himself, and deprives himself of glory and eternal blessedness.
"Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man" (Ps 5:6).
"Blessed is the man unto whom the LORD imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile" (Ps 32:2).
"Keep thy tongue from evil, and thy lips from speaking guile" (Ps 34:13).
"But thou, O God, shalt bring them down into the pit of destruction: bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; but I will trust in thee" (Ps 55:23).
"He that worketh deceit shall not dwell within my house: he that telleth lies shall not tarry in my sight" (Ps 101:7).
"What doth he give thee? or what doth he add unto thee, thou deceitful tongue?" (Ps 120:3).
"A false balance is abomination to the LORD: but a just weight is his delight" (Prov 11:1).
"The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but to him that soweth righteousness shall be a sure reward" (Prov 11:18).
"He that speaketh truth sheweth forth righteousness: but a false witness deceit" (Prov 12:17).
"Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy" (Prov 12:20).
"The wisdom of the prudent is to understand his way: but the folly of fools is deceit" (Prov 14:8).
"A true witness delivereth souls: but he that speaketh lies is deceit" (Prov 14:25).
"Weight and weight is an abomination to the LORD, and deceitful balances are not good" (Prov 20:23).
"The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind" (Prov 21:27).
"He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him" (Prov 26:24).
"For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in" (Wis 1:5).
"Yea, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul" (Wis 4:11).
"Bring not every man into thine house: for the deceitful man hath many trains" (Sir 11:31).

*Do you not speak before the Lord, and utter deceit before Him, despite your splendid words? This is what he wishes to say: you do not believe that God listens to what you say, because deceit dictates your dialogue. No good motive moves you, but the desire to harm my reputation and to make wounding comments. For even if your words are proper, you do not express a good intention by them; they do not seek correction, reform and progress, but seek destruction, for you are not teaching a man who is wholly ignorant.

St. John Chrysostom * [Hath God need of your lie, that ye speak deceitfully for him?] God has no need of a lie, for the truth does not accept being accomplished with the help of falsehood... The heretics speak deceit for Him, deceiving those of weak minds, misleading their concepts of God in a foolish manner.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

In St. Augustine's commentary on (Ps 55:23), he compares the shedders of blood with the deceiving heretics and those who speak deceit, and says that the shedders of blood are manifest murderers who shed the blood of bodies and do not kill souls, whereas the heretics destroy souls and shed their invisible blood. They are bloody and deceitful men!

In his commentary on the Psalmist's question and answer: [What doth he give thee, and what is set before thee against the deceitful tongue? Sharpened arrows of the mighty, with coals of desolation] (Ps 120:3-4), he sees that the opposition to those with deceitful tongues is not by mere words, but requires the word of God, the sharpened arrows of the mighty one, together with living examples of righteous persons who were like a lifeless, desolate desert and became burning like coals. He says: [It is not enough to answer them with words, but we also defend with examples... The word "coals" is used to express examples of many sinners who returned to the Lord. You hear people marveling and saying: "I know a man how addicted to drink he was, how base in his love of theaters and the circus and his love of deceit; now behold, he serves God, how innocent he has become!" Do not marvel, for he has become a living coal. Rejoice that he is alive, he for whom you grieved because he was dead.]
Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God? [8]

God does not need defenders; in their defense they hate their brothers. "Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?" How do they serve God by hatred and loathing of their brothers? In their zeal for God, they insult God and rob Him of the seat of His judgment as the Judge of mankind. For He alone knows every soul and its strength and inclinations, and man's gifts, his biological makeup, his energies and the circumstances surrounding him. On the basis of all this He is the One who condemns or justifies. Truly we may know a man who committed a certain sin, perhaps obvious, needing no investigation; but can we judge the man as a whole because of a sin or sins he committed at one time, when we do not know his depths or his circumstances?!

* [Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?] [8] For when fools see the deeds of the wise, they all appear to them to be worthy of blame. They forget their own emptiness and shortcomings, and judge the conduct of others with greater zeal... On the other hand, when the righteous rebuke the conduct of the wicked, they always acknowledge their own weaknesses and that they themselves deserve blame. For even if they rebuke and rush strongly to resist the evils of others from outside, yet they sympathize with them inwardly, realizing that the examination of men's sins belongs to God... Therefore the friends of blessed Job rebuked his deeds as though they themselves had done nothing blameworthy.

Well was it said here: [Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?] For a person to put on the face of God means that he claims for himself His authority to condemn; and a person contends for God when he rebukes the weak points in others and does not feel his own inward weakness.
Pope Gregory (the Great)

* An elder said: "If no one knows what is in a man save his spirit, as the Apostle says, and if we know that many have repented and we did not know of their repentance, then a man may repent at the end of his life, and be accepted like the repentance of the thief; so you must not judge anyone. For the Judge is God alone, so how can anyone dare to intervene in what belongs to God?!"

The Garden of the Monks * Do not be a judge of your brother, that you may be made worthy of forgiveness. Perhaps you always see him as wrong, but you do not know with what ending he departs the world. The thief crucified with Jesus was a murderer and a shedder of blood, and Judas was a disciple of Christ and among the intimates, since the purse was with him; yet in a short time they changed, so the thief entered Paradise, and the disciple deserved the gallows and perished.

St. Anastasius * Look, my brothers: the work of the servants at the wedding of the king's son (Mt 22) was nothing but drawing the good and the wicked to the feast. The Lord did not say of them that they judged those invited and distinguished between the good and the wicked, nor did He say of them that they found one who did not have a wedding garment; rather the king himself was the one who saw him, the master of the house alone discovered him and cast him out.

St. Augustine * If you see a man who has sinned and you see him on the morrow, do not look at him as a sinner, for you do not know whether in the period of your absence from him he has done something good after the fall; rather, plead with the Lord with sighs and bitter tears, entreating Him!
St. Ephraim the Syrian

9 "Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man is deceived, do ye deceive him? 10 He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons. 11 Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you? 12 Your speeches are like ashes, and your strongholds are strongholds of clay."
Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man is deceived, do ye deceive him? [9]

It is for their good, and better for them, that God should search their hearts and reveal to them their hatred of their brothers and their loathing of the truth, than that they should cloak themselves with an outward defense of God, and so deceive Him (beguile Him unawares) as a man is deceived.

* Every innovator is, in relation to God, "an enemy and a defender," for in his struggle and in the way of his defense of God he resists the truth. But nothing can escape the sight of God, for He judges according to the thoughts of the heart rather than the outward appearance in which he seems to be one who serves God.
Pope Gregory (the Great)
* How do they resist the truth except by the vanity of their pride, exalted in vain? While they set themselves up on high as great and righteous men, they pass away like empty air.

St. Augustine * If anyone objects to the existence of heretics now, let him remember that it has been so from the beginning, since Satan was always setting up error over against the truth. In the beginning God promised good things, and Satan too made his promise. God established Paradise, and Satan deceived man by saying: [Ye shall be as gods] (Gen 3:5); for if he was unable to provide a work, he offered promises which are rather words, and this is the nature of deceivers.
After this came Cain, and with him Abel; the sons of Seth, and with them the daughters of men; Ham, and with him Japheth; Abraham (and in his days) there was Pharaoh; Jacob, and with him Esau.
And so came Moses (and Aaron), and the two magicians arose.
The prophets, and with them the false prophets.
The apostles and the false apostles; Christ, and the Antichrist will come.
This is what was before, and what has happened up to that day... In brief, there was never a time when falsehood did not exist to stand against the truth. So do not be troubled.
St. John Chrysostom He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons [10].

In rebuking Job in this spirit filled with hatred, they became respecters of persons, even if secretly; therefore they are not counted in the eyes of God worthy of praise, but of severe reproof. God abhors the hatred concealed under the defense of God and of His glory and Kingdom. Perhaps by respect of persons he meant that they used to honor him, perhaps with exaggeration, for his wealth, and for no reason their conduct completely changed when he became poor and lost his social position and his authority as a king or leader, and also all his money. Scripture has warned us against partiality.
"Wherefore now let the fear of the LORD be upon you; take heed and do it: for there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of gifts" (2 Chr 19:7).
"These things also belong to the wise. It is not good to have respect of persons in judgment" (Prov 24:23).
"To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress" (Prov 28:21).
"For there is no respect of persons with God" (Rom 2:11).
"And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him" (Eph 6:9).
"But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done: and there is no respect of persons" (Col 3:25).
"I charge thee before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, and the elect angels, that thou observe these things without preferring one before another, doing nothing by partiality" (1 Tim 5:21).
"My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons" (Jas 2:1).
"And if ye call on the Father, who without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning here in fear" (1 Pet 1:17).

Pope Gregory (the Great) says that God is the searcher of the secrets of hearts and nothing is hidden from Him (1 Cor 4:5); for it may happen that under the cover of defending the truth, some blame the righteous man, and show partiality to those who stand against the righteous, while they stand on the side of those who blaspheme God. These claim that they glorify God, while they bear no sincerity in their conduct. They are like the demons who said to the Lord Christ: [Thou art the Son of God] (Mk 3:11); in this they do not seek His glory, but are terrified of what will come upon them.

* What benefit comes to you from honoring (showing partiality to) the rich man? Is it because he is better prepared to keep the love of others for him? So we do kindness to those from whom we expect that they will repay us for it. We must think rather of the weak and needy, because for the sake of these we hope for recompense from the Lord Jesus, who in the example of the wedding feast (Lk 14:12-13) gave us a general picture of virtue. For He asked us to give our works rather to those who are not able to repay us.
* If the Kingdom of God is for the poor, who is richer than they?
St. Ambrose * All are equal before God; only the rank of each is raised according to his faith, and not according to his money.
St. Augustine * Many rebuke me, saying: You are always pressing hard on the rich, and they in turn press hard on the poor.

Well, I do press hard on the rich, or rather not on the rich, but on those who misuse money. I do not attack their persons but their greed. Wealth is one thing, and greed is another; having a surplus is one thing, and covetousness is another.
Are you rich? I do not forbid you this. Be rich. Are you greedy? I warn you... I will not be silent.

Do you attack me because of this? I am ready for my blood to be shed, but I want to keep you from sinning. I bear you no hatred, nor do I wage war on you, but I want one thing only, the benefit of those who listen to me.
